title: कप्पसुत्त — जिणचरिय
titleEn: The Kalpasūtra — Life of Mahāvīra 1: The Descent and the Dreams (§§1–4)
part: 1 · The Namokkāra; the Descent and the Dreams (§§1–4)
source: Text: Hermann Jacobi, The Kalpasûtra of Bhadrabâhu (Leipzig: Brockhaus, 1879; Abhandlungen für die Kunde des Morgenlandes VII.1), Jinacaritra, the Namokkāra and §§1–4 (pp. 33–34), transcribed from the Wellcome Collection scan (public domain). Section numbers are Jacobi’s. Jacobi prints the Prakrit in Roman letters; the romanization under each word is his, put into IAST (â î û → ā ī ū; his dotted ọ, an o formed by contraction, → o), with his hyphens between compound members, his apostrophes for elided vowels, his brackets and his punctuation. The Devanagari is converted letter for letter from it, compounds closed up as Prakrit is printed in India; a vowel after a vowel keeps its own letter, since this Prakrit has no diphthongs. Round brackets: words missing in Jacobi’s manuscript A; square brackets: words missing in manuscripts A and C. His footnotes of variant readings are not reproduced. Pronunciation: not yet chosen (no audio). Translations made fresh from the Prakrit for Lectorium; no translation consulted for wording.
about: The Kalpasūtra, ascribed by tradition to Bhadrabāhu, is among the best-loved scriptures of the Śvetāmbara Jains: monks read it aloud to the community every year during the festival of Paryuṣaṇa. Its first and longest part, the Jinacaritra, tells the lives of the Jinas, beginning with Mahāvīra, the twenty-fourth and last of this age. This opening has the Namokkāra, the salutation every Jain knows by heart; the five great moments of Mahāvīra’s life; his descent from heaven into the womb of the brahmin woman Devānandā; and the fourteen dreams she sees that night.

sentences.t: नमो अरिहंताणं नमो सिद्धाणं नमो आयरियाणं नमो उवज्झायाणं नमो लोए सव्वसाहूणं ।
sentences.tr: Namo arihaṃtāṇaṃ namo siddhāṇaṃ namo āyariyāṇaṃ namo uvajjhāyāṇaṃ namo loe savva-sāhūṇaṃ.
sentences.l: Homage to-the-Arhats, homage to-the-Siddhas, homage to-the-Ācāryas, homage to-the-Upādhyāyas, homage in-the-world to-all-the-sādhus.

morph.gloss: Arhat, a Jina: one who has conquered the passions and teaches while still in the body (gen. pl.)
Siddha, a soul that is perfected and freed from the body for ever (gen. pl.)
Ācārya, a head of a monastic order (gen. pl.)
Upādhyāya, a monk who teaches the scriptures (gen. pl.)

sentences.i: Homage to the Arhats, homage to the Siddhas, homage to the Ācāryas, homage to the Upādhyāyas, homage to all the sādhus in the world.
sentences.n: The Namokkāra (Sanskrit Namaskāra), the salutation every Jain knows by heart, to the five supreme beings: Arhats, enlightened teachers still living in a body; Siddhas, liberated souls; Ācāryas, heads of the monastic orders; Upādhyāyas, teachers of scripture; and all monks. It names no person, only kinds of holiness. Grammar: namo takes the genitive (-āṇaṃ, Sanskrit -ānām), because Prakrit has lost the dative and uses the genitive in its place. Jacobi notes that manuscript M lacks this opening blessing.

sentences.t:
एसो पंचनमोक्कारो सव्वपावप्पणासणो ।
मंगलाणं च सव्वेसिं पढमं हवइ मंगलं ॥
sentences.tr:
eso paṃca-namokkāro savva-pāva-ppaṇāsaṇo
maṃgalāṇaṃ ca savvesiṃ paḍhamaṃ havai maṃgalaṃ.
sentences.l:
This five-salutation all-evil-destroying,
and of-blessings of-all first is blessing.

morph.gloss: destroying (nom. sg.; pp doubled at the compound seam)
to be, become (havai: pres. 3 sg., Skt bhavati)

sentences.i: This fivefold salutation destroys all evil, and of all blessings it is the first blessing.
sentences.n: The verse that closes the Namokkāra in daily recitation. Here you can watch Prakrit sound changes at work: eso for Sanskrit eṣaḥ (-aḥ becomes -o), pāva for pāpa (a p between vowels softens to v), havai for bhavati (bh becomes h, and the t between vowels drops out). That last change, the loss of a consonant between vowels, is everywhere in this text.

sentences.t: तेणं कालेणं तेणं समएणं समणे भगवं महावीरे पंचहत्थुत्तरे होत्था ।
sentences.tr: Teṇaṃ kāleṇaṃ teṇaṃ samaeṇaṃ samaṇe bhagavaṃ Mahāvīre paṃca-hatth’uttare hotthā;
sentences.l: In-that time, in-that occasion the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra five-Hastottarā was;

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)
Hastottarā, the lunar mansion after Hasta, i.e. Uttaraphalgunī (nom. sg. masc., 'having five events in Hastottarā')

sentences.i: In that age, at that time, the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, had five events under the asterism Hastottarā:
sentences.n: Teṇaṃ kāleṇaṃ teṇaṃ samaeṇaṃ opens narrative after narrative in the Jain scriptures, as 'once upon a time' does in English. The instrumental (-eṇaṃ) is used for time. Note the nominative in -e (samaṇe, Mahāvīre) where Sanskrit has -aḥ: this is the eastern ending typical of Ardhamāgadhī, and you'll see it constantly. Hastottarā, 'the one after Hasta', is one of the 27 lunar mansions; events are dated by the mansion the moon stands in.

sentences.t: तं जहा । हत्थुत्तराहिं चुए, चइत्ता गब्भं वक्कंते,
sentences.tr: taṃ jahā: hatth’uttarāhiṃ cue, caittā gabbhaṃ vakkaṃte,
sentences.l: that as-follows: with-Hastottarā fell, having-fallen womb entered,

morph.gloss: the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)

sentences.i: namely, under Hastottarā he descended from heaven, and having descended he entered a womb;
sentences.n: Taṃ jahā (Sanskrit tad yathā) introduces a list. Cue, 'fallen', is the regular word for a god's soul leaving heaven when its life there ends. The gerund in -ittā (caittā, 'having fallen') is the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit -tvā; it strings actions together. The asterism is plural in form, hence the instrumental plural hatth’uttarāhiṃ.

sentences.t: हत्थुत्तराहिं गब्भाओ गब्भं साहरिए,
sentences.tr: hatth’uttarāhiṃ gabbhāo gabbhaṃ sāharie,
sentences.l: with-Hastottarā from-womb to-womb was-transferred,

morph.gloss: the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)

sentences.i: under Hastottarā he was carried from one womb to another;
sentences.n: The second event: the transfer of the embryo, which the text tells at length later. In the Śvetāmbara account the god Śakra has the embryo moved from the brahmin woman Devānandā to the warrior-class queen Triśalā, since a Jina is born into a warrior family. The Digambaras reject the story. Ablative in -āo, Sanskrit -āt.

sentences.t: हत्थुत्तराहिं जाए,
sentences.tr: hatth’uttarāhiṃ jāe,
sentences.l: with-Hastottarā was-born,

morph.gloss: the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)

sentences.i: under Hastottarā he was born;
sentences.n: Jāe is Sanskrit jātaḥ: the t between vowels drops out and -aḥ becomes -e. Keep both changes in mind and many words in this text will become recognisable.

sentences.t: हत्थुत्तराहिं मुंडे भवित्ता अगाराओ अणगारियं पव्वइए,
sentences.tr: hatth’uttarāhiṃ muṃḍe bhavittā agārāo aṇagāriyaṃ pavvaie,
sentences.l: with-Hastottarā shaven having-become, from-home into-homelessness went-forth,

morph.gloss: the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)
houselessness, the life of a wandering monk (acc. sg.)
gone forth, become a monk (nom. sg.)

sentences.i: under Hastottarā he had his head shaved and went forth from home into homelessness;
sentences.n: The third event, his renunciation. Muṃḍa bhavittā, 'having become shaven', refers to the removal of the hair at initiation. Agārāo aṇagāriyaṃ pavvaie, 'went forth from the house into houselessness', is the standard phrase for becoming a monk; the same idiom appears in Buddhist texts.

sentences.t: हत्थुत्तराहिं अणंते अणुत्तरे निव्वाघाए निरावरणे कसिणे पडिपुन्ने केवलवरनाणदंसणे समुप्पन्ने ।
sentences.tr: hatth’uttarāhiṃ aṇaṃte aṇuttare nivvāghāe nirāvaraṇe kasiṇe paḍipunne kevala-vara-nāṇa-daṃsaṇe samuppanne;
sentences.l: with-Hastottarā endless, unsurpassed, unobstructed, unveiled, whole, complete, the-kevala-supreme-knowledge-and-perception arose;

morph.gloss: the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)
without a veil, unveiled (nom. sg. neut.)

sentences.i: under Hastottarā there arose in him kevala, the supreme knowledge and perception: infinite, unsurpassed, unobstructed, unveiled, whole and complete;
sentences.n: The fourth event, his enlightenment. Kevala-nāṇa, knowledge that is 'sole' or 'absolute', is omniscience: the soul's own knowing, with nothing left of the karma that covers it (nirāvaraṇa, 'unveiled', names the absence of those covering karmas). Jain doctrine pairs knowledge (nāṇa) with perception (daṃsaṇa) as the soul's two capacities. In Ardhamāgadhī the neuter nominative also ends in -e, so here the subject is a neuter noun.

sentences.t: साइणा परिनिव्वुए भयवं ।
sentences.tr: sāiṇā parinivvue bhayavaṃ.
sentences.l: with-Svāti attained-final-nirvāṇa the-Blessed.

morph.gloss: Svāti, a lunar mansion, two after Hasta (instr. sg.)
completely extinguished, gone to final liberation (nom. sg.)
the Blessed One (nom. sg.; the same word as bhagavaṃ)

sentences.i: Under Svāti the Blessed One reached final liberation.
sentences.n: The fifth event breaks the pattern: Mahāvīra's death and liberation fall under a different lunar mansion, Svāti. Parinivvue, 'wholly extinguished', is the Prakrit form of parinirvṛta. Bhayavaṃ is bhagavaṃ with its g softened to a y sound between vowels; Jacobi keeps both spellings as the manuscripts have them.

sentences.t: तेणं कालेणं तेणं समएणं समणे भगवं महावीरे,
sentences.tr: teṇaṃ kāleṇaṃ teṇaṃ samaeṇaṃ samaṇe bhagavaṃ Mahāvīre,
sentences.l: In-that time, in-that occasion the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra,

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)

sentences.i: In that age, at that time, the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One,
sentences.n: The opening formula again, and the subject of §2 — which has to wait through a very long string of datings and descriptions for its verb, vakkaṃte, 'descended', at the very end of the section. Jain canonical prose likes to pile up phrases before a single finite verb; read on, holding the subject in mind.

sentences.t: जे से गिम्हाणं चउत्थे मासे अट्ठमे पक्खे आसाढसुद्धे,
sentences.tr: je se gimhāṇaṃ cautthe māse aṭṭhame pakkhe āsāḍha-suddhe,
sentences.l: which that of-the-hot-season in-the-fourth month, in-the-eighth fortnight, in-Āṣāḍha-bright,

morph.gloss: that, he (se: nom. sg. masc., Skt saḥ)
fortnight, half of a lunar month (loc. sg.)
bright, i.e. the waxing half (loc. sg.)

sentences.i: in the fourth month of the hot season, the eighth fortnight, the bright half of Āṣāḍha,
sentences.n: Je se, 'which that', is a stock way of introducing a date, picked up by tassa ṇaṃ in the next unit. The hot season has four months, so its fourth month, Āṣāḍha, holds its eighth fortnight; suddha, 'bright', is the half of the month when the moon waxes.

sentences.t: तस्स णं आसाढसुद्धस्स छट्ठीपक्खेणं महाविजयपुप्फुत्तरपवरपुंडरीयाओ महाविमाणाओ वीसंसागरोवमट्ठितीयाओ
sentences.tr: tassa ṇaṃ āsāḍha-suddhassa chaṭṭhī-pakkheṇaṃ mahāvijaya-pupph’uttara-pavara-puṃḍarīyāo mahāvimāṇāo vīsaṃ-sāgarovama-ṭṭhitīyāo
sentences.l: of-that, ṇaṃ, Āṣāḍha-bright on-the-sixth-day, from-the-great-victory-Puṣpottara-excellent-lotus great-heavenly-palace twenty-ocean-measures-lasting,

morph.gloss: an emphatic particle with no English equivalent
fortnight (instr. sg.: 'on the sixth day of the fortnight')
Puṣpottara, the heavenly palace Mahāvīra came from
white lotus; the finest of its kind (abl. sg.)
heavenly palace, celestial dwelling of the gods (abl. sg.)
an 'ocean-measure', an immense unit of time

sentences.i: on its sixth day, from Puṣpottara, the great heavenly palace of great victory, the finest lotus of them all, where life lasts twenty ocean-measures,
sentences.n: Ṇaṃ is a small emphatic particle that Ardhamāgadhī prose sprinkles everywhere; it adds nothing translatable, so read past it. A sāgarovama, 'ocean-measure', is a period of time beyond counting; Jain cosmology measures the lives of the gods in them. The long compound is a list of epithets of the palace in the ablative (-āo, 'from'); the -ṭṭh- doubles at the compound seam.

sentences.t: (आउक्खएणं भवक्खएणं ठिइक्खएणं) अणंतरं चयं चइत्ता
sentences.tr: (āu-kkhaeṇaṃ bhava-kkhaeṇaṃ ṭhii-kkhaeṇaṃ) aṇaṃtaraṃ cayaṃ caittā
sentences.l: (by-life-ending, by-existence-ending, by-stay-ending) immediately descent having-descended
sentences.i: (when his lifespan, his existence as a god and his stay there had run out,) he descended straight away,
sentences.n: Jacobi prints the three phrases in round brackets because manuscript A lacks them; one commentary marks them as found only in some copies. Cayaṃ caittā, 'having fallen a fall', pairs a verb with its own noun for emphasis. The god's soul descends the instant its heavenly life is used up: there is no interval (aṇaṃtaraṃ) between one existence and the next.

sentences.t: इहेव जंबुद्दीवे दीवे भारहे वासे इमीसे ओसप्पिणीए
sentences.tr: ih’ eva Jaṃbuddīve dīve Bhārahe vāse imīse osappiṇīe
sentences.l: right-here in-the-Jambū continent, in-the-Bhārata land, in-this descending-age,

morph.gloss: Jambūdvīpa, 'rose-apple continent', the central continent of the world (loc. sg.)
Bhārata, the southern region of Jambūdvīpa: India (loc. sg.)
the descending half of the cycle of time (loc. sg.)

sentences.i: here in the continent of Jambūdvīpa, in the land of Bhārata, in this present descending age,
sentences.n: Jain cosmography places our world on Jambūdvīpa, a ring-shaped central continent; Bhārata is its southern land, India. Time turns in endless cycles, each half divided into six eras; in the descending half (osappiṇī, Sanskrit avasarpiṇī) everything slowly declines. The locatives in -e and the feminine locative in -īe set the scene.

sentences.t: सुसमसुसमाए समाए विइक्कंताए सुसमाए समाए विइक्कंताए सुसमदुस्समाए समाए विइक्कंताए दुस्समसुसमाए समाए बहुविइक्कंताए [सागरोवमकोडाकोडीए बायालीसाए वाससहस्सेहिं ऊणियाए]
sentences.tr: susama-susamāe samāe viikkaṃtāe susamāe samāe viikkaṃtāe susama-dussamāe samāe viikkaṃtāe dussama-susamāe samāe bahu-viikkaṃtāe [sāgarovama-koḍākoḍīe bāyālīsāe vāsa-sahassehiṃ ūṇiyāe]
sentences.l: the-happy-happy era having-passed, the-happy era having-passed, the-happy-unhappy era having-passed, the-unhappy-happy era much-having-passed [a-crore-of-crores-of-ocean-measures by-forty-two year-thousands lacking]

morph.gloss: happiness; doubled, susama-susamā, 'happy-happy', the first and best era (loc. sg.)
a crore of crores, a hundred million million (loc. sg.)

sentences.i: when the 'very happy' era had passed, and the 'happy' era, and the 'happy-unhappy' era, and most of the 'unhappy-happy' era had gone by [an era of a hundred million million ocean-measures, less forty-two thousand years],
sentences.n: A chain of locative absolutes, 'the era having passed': four of the six eras of the descending half, named by their balance of happiness (susamā) and misery (dussamā). The fourth era, in which all twenty-four Jinas of this cycle live, is the one now nearly over. Jacobi puts the bracketed phrase in square brackets because manuscripts A and C lack it and B has it only in the margin.

sentences.t: पंचहत्तरीए वासेहिं अद्धनवमेहि य मासेहिं सेसेहिं
sentences.tr: paṃca-hattarīe vāsehiṃ addha-navamehi ya māsehiṃ sesehiṃ
sentences.l: seventy-five years and eight-and-a-half months remaining,

morph.gloss: ninth; addha-navama, 'with the ninth half', eight and a half (instr. pl.)

sentences.i: with seventy-five years and eight and a half months of it still to run,
sentences.n: Addha-navama, 'half-ninth', means eight and a half: the ninth month counts only by half. The same idiom exists in Sanskrit and Pali. Ya is ca, 'and', with its c dropped between vowels and a y sound bridging the gap. An instrumental absolute: 'with seventy-five years remaining'.

sentences.t: एक्कवीसाए तित्थयरेहिं इक्खागकुलसमुप्पन्नेहिं कासवगोत्तेहिं दोहि य हरिवंसकुलसमुप्पन्नेहिं गोयमसगोत्तेहिं तेवीसाए तित्थयरेहिं विइक्कंतेहिं
sentences.tr: ekka-vīsāe titthayarehiṃ Ikkhāga-kula-samuppannehiṃ Kāsava-gottehiṃ dohi ya Harivaṃsa-kula-samuppannehiṃ Goyama-sagottehiṃ tevīsāe titthayarehiṃ viikkaṃtehiṃ
sentences.l: twenty-one Tīrthaṅkaras Ikṣvāku-family-born of-Kāśyapa-clan, and two Harivaṃśa-family-born of-Gautama-clan, twenty-three Tīrthaṅkaras having-passed,
sentences.i: after twenty-three Tīrthaṅkaras had come and gone, twenty-one of them born in the Ikṣvāku family, of the Kāśyapa clan, and two born in the Harivaṃśa family, of the Gautama clan,
sentences.n: Titthayara, 'ford-maker', is the Jain title for a Jina: one who makes a crossing (tittha) over the ocean of rebirth for others to follow. Mahāvīra is the twenty-fourth and last of this cycle. The two of the Harivaṃśa family are Munisuvrata and Nemi, the twentieth and twenty-second. Another instrumental absolute, closing the long dating.

sentences.t: समणे भगवं महावीरे चरिमे तित्थयरे पुव्वतित्थयरनिद्दिट्ठे
sentences.tr: samaṇe bhagavaṃ Mahāvīre carime titthayare puvva-titthayara-niddiṭṭhe
sentences.l: the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra, the-last Tīrthaṅkara, by-former-Tīrthaṅkaras-foretold,

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)

sentences.i: the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, the last Tīrthaṅkara, whose coming the earlier Tīrthaṅkaras had foretold,
sentences.n: After the dating the subject is repeated, so the reader can find the thread again. Carima, 'last', is a title as much as a description: with him the line of twenty-four is complete.

sentences.t: माहणकुंडग्गामे नयरे उसभदत्तस्स माहणस्स कोडालसगोत्तस्स भारियाए देवाणंदाए माहणीए जालंधरसगोत्ताए
sentences.tr: māhaṇa-Kuṃḍaggāme nayare Usabhadattassa māhaṇassa Koḍāla-sagottassa bhāriyāe Devāṇaṃdāe māhaṇīe Jālaṃdhara-sagottāe
sentences.l: in-the-brahmin-Kuṇḍagrāma town, of-Ṛṣabhadatta the-brahmin of-the-Koḍāla-clan, of-the-wife Devānandā the-brahmin-woman of-the-Jālandhara-clan,

morph.gloss: Kuṇḍagrāma, a town near Vaiśālī (loc. sg.: 'in Brahmin Kuṇḍagrāma')
belonging to the clan (gen. sg. fem.)

sentences.i: in the town of Brahmin Kuṇḍagrāma, into the womb of Devānandā, brahmin wife of the brahmin Ṛṣabhadatta, he of the Koḍāla clan and she of the Jālandhara clan,
sentences.n: Kuṇḍagrāma had a brahmin quarter and a warrior quarter; the embryo will later be moved from one to the other. Māhaṇa is the Ardhamāgadhī form of brāhmaṇa. The feminine genitive ends in -āe or -īe, the same as the locative: these genitives depend on kucchiṃsi, 'in the womb', which comes two units later.

sentences.t: पुव्वरत्तावरत्तकालसमयंसि हत्थुत्तराहिं नक्खत्तेणं जोगमुवागएणं
sentences.tr: puvva-rattāvaratta-kāla-samayaṃsi hatth’uttarāhiṃ nakkhatteṇaṃ jogam uvāgaeṇaṃ
sentences.l: at-the-first-night-latter-night-time-moment, with-Hastottarā the-asterism conjunction having-come-to,

morph.gloss: the first part of the night
the latter part of the night
time, moment (loc. sg.: 'at the moment between the two halves of the night', midnight)
the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)
conjunction, union (acc. sg.; m kept before a vowel)

sentences.i: at midnight, when the moon had come into conjunction with the asterism Hastottarā,
sentences.n: Puvva-ratta-avaratta, 'the first night and the later night', is the moment where they meet: midnight. The locative in -aṃsi (Sanskrit -asmin) is distinctive of Ardhamāgadhī; you'll see it constantly. Jogam uvāgaeṇaṃ, 'having come into union', is said of the asterism meeting the moon; the m of jogam is kept before the following vowel and the two words are written together in Devanagari.

sentences.t: आहारवक्कंतीए भववक्कंतीए सरीरवक्कंतीए कुच्छिंसि गब्भत्ताए वक्कंते ।
sentences.tr: āhāra-vakkaṃtīe bhava-vakkaṃtīe sarīra-vakkaṃtīe kucchiṃsi gabbhattāe vakkaṃte.
sentences.l: with-food-descent, with-existence-descent, with-body-descent, in-the-womb as-embryo descended.

morph.gloss: the state of an embryo (instr./dat. sg.: 'as an embryo')

sentences.i: descended into her womb as an embryo, taking on a new nourishment, a new existence and a new body.
sentences.n: Here at last is the verb of §2, vakkaṃte, 'descended'. The three vakkaṃti phrases name what changes when a soul passes from heaven into a womb: what feeds it, what kind of existence it has, and what body it wears. Gabbhattāe, 'into embryo-hood', uses the abstract suffix -ttā (Sanskrit -tā).

sentences.t: समणे भगवं महावीरे तिण्णाणोवगए आवि होत्था ।
sentences.tr: samaṇe bhagavaṃ Mahāvīre tiṇ-ṇāṇovagae āvi hotthā.
sentences.l: The-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra, three-knowledge-possessed even was.

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)
possessed of (nom. sg.: 'possessed of three kinds of knowledge')

sentences.i: The ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, had three kinds of knowledge.
sentences.n: Jain teaching counts five kinds of knowledge: through the senses, through scripture, clairvoyance, knowledge of others' minds, and omniscience. A future Jina is born with the first three; the fourth comes when he becomes a monk, and the fifth, omniscience, at his enlightenment. Ṇāṇa + uvagaa contract to -ṇovagae, the o that Jacobi marks with a dot.

sentences.t: ‘चइस्सामि’ त्ति जाणइ, चयमाणे न जाणइ, ‘चुए ’मि’ त्ति जाणइ ।
sentences.tr: ‘caissāmi’ tti jāṇai, cayamāṇe na jāṇai, ‘cue ’mi’ tti jāṇai.
sentences.l: ‘I-shall-descend’ thus he-knows, descending not he-knows, ‘descended I-am’ thus he-knows.

morph.gloss: to fall, descend (caissāmi: fut. 1 sg., 'I shall descend')
I am (amhi/ammi with the a elided)

sentences.i: He knew, ‘I am going to descend’; while he was descending he did not know it; he knew, ‘I have descended.’
sentences.n: The present jāṇai, 'knows', tells a past event, as English can say 'he knows' in a story. Tti (Sanskrit iti) marks the words in quotation marks as his thought. Jain commentators explain the middle clause as follows: the descent takes a single instant, the smallest unit of time, too brief for any knowledge short of omniscience to grasp.

sentences.t: जं रयणिं च णं समणे भगवं महावीरे देवाणंदाए माहणीए जालंधरसगोत्ताए कुच्छिंसि गब्भत्ताए वक्कंते,
sentences.tr: jaṃ rayaṇiṃ ca ṇaṃ samaṇe bhagavaṃ Mahāvīre Devāṇaṃdāe māhaṇīe Jālaṃdhara-sagottāe kucchiṃsi gabbhattāe vakkaṃte,
sentences.l: On-which night ṇaṃ the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra into-the-womb of-Devānandā the-brahmin-woman of-the-Jālandhara-clan as-embryo descended,

morph.gloss: an emphatic particle with no English equivalent
the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)
belonging to the clan (gen. sg. fem.)
the state of an embryo (instr./dat. sg.: 'as an embryo')

sentences.i: On the night when the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, descended as an embryo into the womb of Devānandā, the brahmin woman of the Jālandhara clan,
sentences.n: Jaṃ rayaṇiṃ ... taṃ rayaṇiṃ, 'on which night ... on that night': a relative clause answered by a correlative, the usual Indic way of building such a sentence. The accusative marks a stretch of time. The whole clause repeats the words of §2 almost exactly; repetition of this kind is part of the text's style.

sentences.t: तं रयणिं च णं सा देवाणंदा माहणी सयणिज्जंसि सुत्तजागरा ओहीरमाणी
sentences.tr: taṃ rayaṇiṃ ca ṇaṃ sā Devāṇaṃdā māhaṇī sayaṇijjaṃsi sutta-jāgarā ohīramāṇī
sentences.l: on-that night ṇaṃ she Devānandā the-brahmin-woman on-the-bed asleep-awake dozing

morph.gloss: an emphatic particle with no English equivalent
awake (nom. sg. fem.: 'between sleep and waking')
to doze, nod off (ohīramāṇī: pres. participle, nom. sg. fem.; the word is rare and its origin uncertain)

sentences.i: that night the brahmin woman Devānandā, lying on her bed between sleep and waking, drowsing,
sentences.n: Sutta-jāgarā, 'asleep-awake', is the half-conscious state in which, in Indian tradition, prophetic dreams come. Ohīramāṇī, 'dozing', is a rare word whose origin is uncertain; its sense is clear from the context and from the commentaries. Another locative in -aṃsi: sayaṇijjaṃsi, 'on the bed'.

sentences.t: इमे एयारूवे ओराले कल्लाणे सिवे धन्ने मंगल्ले सस्सिरीए चोद्दस महासुमिणे पासित्ता णं पडिबुद्धा ।
sentences.tr: ime eyārūve orāle kallāṇe sive dhanne maṃgalle sassirīe coddasa mahāsumiṇe pāsittā ṇaṃ paḍibuddhā.
sentences.l: these such-formed grand, fortunate, propitious, prosperous, blessed, glorious fourteen great-dreams having-seen ṇaṃ awoke.

morph.gloss: an emphatic particle with no English equivalent

sentences.i: saw these fourteen great dreams, splendid, fortunate, propitious, prosperous, blessed and glorious, and awoke.
sentences.n: The mother of every Tīrthaṅkara sees fourteen great dreams on the night of his conception (Digambaras count sixteen). The masculine accusative plural ends in -e in Ardhamāgadhī, the same as the nominative singular, so the endings alone will not tell you which you have: the verb pāsittā, 'having seen', settles it. Sumiṇa is Sanskrit svapna, with a vowel inserted to break up the consonant cluster.

sentences.t: तं जहा,
sentences.tr: taṃ jahā,
sentences.l: That as-follows,
sentences.i: They were these:
sentences.n: Taṃ jahā again introduces a list. What follows is a verse, the traditional memory-verse naming the fourteen dreams in order.

sentences.t:
गय वसह सीह अभिसेय
दाम ससि दिणयरं झयं कुंभं ।
पउमसर सागर विमाण-
भवण रयणुच्चय सिहिं च ॥
sentences.tr:
gaya vasaha sīha abhiseya
dāma sasi diṇayaraṃ jhayaṃ kuṃbhaṃ
paumasara sāgara vimāṇa-
bhavaṇa rayaṇ’-uccaya sihiṃ ca.
sentences.l:
elephant, bull, lion, anointing,
garland, moon, sun, banner, jar,
lotus-lake, ocean, palace-
dwelling, jewel-heap and flame.

morph.gloss: anointing; here the anointing of the goddess Śrī
dwelling, palace (vimāṇa-bhavaṇa: a heavenly palace, or the palace of the gods below the earth)

sentences.i: An elephant, a bull, a lion, the anointing of the goddess Śrī, a garland, the moon, the sun, a banner, a jar, a lotus lake, the ocean, a heavenly palace, a heap of jewels and a flame.
sentences.n: The fourteen dreams in their canonical order, in the old āryā metre, which counts syllable lengths rather than syllables. Most items are bare stems with no ending, as in a list; a few take the accusative (diṇayaraṃ, jhayaṃ, kuṃbhaṃ, sihiṃ), the dreams being what she saw. Vimāṇa-bhavaṇa is split across the line: the tradition explains that a mother whose son comes down from heaven sees a heavenly palace (vimāṇa), and one whose son comes up from below sees a palace of the underworld gods (bhavaṇa).

glossary.माहणीए: māhaṇīe — māhaṇī (Skt brāhmaṇī) — brahmin woman (gen. sg.)
glossary.जालंधरसगोत्ताए: Jālaṃdhara-sagottāe — Jālaṃdhara — the Jālandhara clan; sagotta — belonging to the clan (gen. sg. fem.)
glossary.पुव्वरत्तावरत्तकालसमयंसि: puvva-rattāvaratta-kāla-samayaṃsi — puvva-ratta (Skt pūrva-rātra) — the first part of the night; avaratta (Skt apara-rātra) — the latter part of the night; kāla-samaya — time, moment (loc. sg.: 'at the moment between the two halves of the night', midnight)
glossary.नक्खत्तेणं: nakkhatteṇaṃ — nakkhatta (Skt nakṣatra) — lunar mansion, asterism (instr. sg.)
glossary.जोगमुवागएणं: jogam uvāgaeṇaṃ — joga (Skt yoga) — conjunction, union (acc. sg.; m kept before a vowel); uvāgaa (Skt upāgata) — come to (instr. sg.)
glossary.आहारवक्कंतीए: āhāra-vakkaṃtīe — āhāra — food, nourishment; vakkaṃti (Skt avakrānti) — descent, entry (instr. sg.)
glossary.भववक्कंतीए: bhava-vakkaṃtīe — bhava — existence, birth; vakkaṃti — descent (instr. sg.)
glossary.सरीरवक्कंतीए: sarīra-vakkaṃtīe — sarīra (Skt śarīra) — body; vakkaṃti — descent (instr. sg.)
glossary.कुच्छिंसि: kucchiṃsi — kucchi (Skt kukṣi) — belly, womb (loc. sg.)
glossary.गब्भत्ताए: gabbhattāe — gabbhattā (Skt garbhatā) — the state of an embryo (instr./dat. sg.: 'as an embryo')
glossary.तिण्णाणोवगए: tiṇ-ṇāṇovagae — ti (Skt tri) — three; ṇāṇa — knowledge; uvagaa (Skt upagata) — possessed of (nom. sg.: 'possessed of three kinds of knowledge')
glossary.चइस्सामि: caissāmi — cay / cu — to fall, descend (caissāmi: fut. 1 sg., 'I shall descend')
glossary.त्ति: tti — tti (Skt iti) — thus (closes a quotation)
glossary.जाणइ: jāṇai — jāṇ (Skt jñā) — to know (jāṇai: pres. 3 sg.)
glossary.चयमाणे: cayamāṇe — cayamāṇa — descending (pres. participle, nom. sg.)
glossary.मि: mi — ’mi (Skt asmi) — I am (amhi/ammi with the a elided)
glossary.जं: jaṃ — ja — which (jaṃ: acc. sg. fem.)
glossary.सा: sā — ta — that, she (sā: nom. sg. fem.)
glossary.सयणिज्जंसि: sayaṇijjaṃsi — sayaṇijja (Skt śayanīya) — bed, couch (loc. sg.)
glossary.सुत्तजागरा: sutta-jāgarā — sutta (Skt supta) — asleep; jāgara — awake (nom. sg. fem.: 'between sleep and waking')
glossary.ओहीरमाणी: ohīramāṇī — ohīr — to doze, nod off (ohīramāṇī: pres. participle, nom. sg. fem.; the word is rare and its origin uncertain)
glossary.इमे: ime — ima — this (ime: acc. pl. masc.)
glossary.एयारूवे: eyārūve — eyārūva (Skt etad-rūpa) — of such a kind (acc. pl.)
glossary.ओराले: orāle — orāla (Skt udāra) — grand, splendid (acc. pl.)
glossary.कल्लाणे: kallāṇe — kallāṇa (Skt kalyāṇa) — fortunate, lovely (acc. pl.)
glossary.धन्ने: dhanne — dhanna (Skt dhanya) — bringing wealth, prosperous (acc. pl.)
glossary.मंगल्ले: maṃgalle — maṃgalla (Skt māṅgalya) — auspicious, blessed (acc. pl.)
glossary.महासुमिणे: mahāsumiṇe — mahā — great; sumiṇa (Skt svapna) — dream (acc. pl.)
glossary.पासित्ता: pāsittā — pās (Skt paś) — to see (pāsittā: gerund, 'having seen')
glossary.पडिबुद्धा: paḍibuddhā — paḍibuddha (Skt pratibuddha) — awakened (nom. sg. fem.)
glossary.अभिसेय: abhiseya — abhiseya (Skt abhiṣeka) — anointing; here the anointing of the goddess Śrī
glossary.दिणयरं: diṇayaraṃ — diṇayara (Skt dinakara) — 'day-maker', the sun (acc. sg.)
glossary.कुंभं: kuṃbhaṃ — kuṃbha (Skt kumbha) — jar, pitcher (acc. sg.)
glossary.पउमसर: paumasara — pauma (Skt padma) — lotus; sara (Skt saras) — lake: 'lotus lake'
glossary.भवण: bhavaṇa — bhavaṇa (Skt bhavana) — dwelling, palace (vimāṇa-bhavaṇa: a heavenly palace, or the palace of the gods below the earth)
glossary.रयणुच्चय: rayaṇ’-uccaya — rayaṇa (Skt ratna) — jewel; uccaya — heap: 'heap of jewels'
glossary.सिहिं: sihiṃ — sihi (Skt śikhin) — fire, flame (acc. sg.)
